newsitem.title: USA: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. December S&P 500 futures finish higher.

text.p: U.S. December Standard and Poor's 500 futures finished higher after hitting a 10-week high during the day on Treasury bond strength.
A benign producer price report for August dampened rate-hike fears and boosted December Treasury bonds. Stocks followed suit.
August PPI rose 0.3 percent overall but fell 0.1 percent excluding the volatile food and energy sectors. Wall Street forecasts had been for a 0.1 percent gain in both components.
The tame core rate stirred ideas that perhaps inflation was being kept at bay, even amid good economic growth.
August consumer prices will be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT on Friday and were forecast up 0.2 percent in both core and overall rates. In July, both core and overall CPI rose 0.3 percent.

"The market continues to work higher and they liked the numbers this morning, although we had one little scare in the afternoon when we had a story about Iraq shooting at American planes," an S&P 500 futures trader said.
Tensions mounted between the U.S. and Iraq, though traders said nervousness would have to be sustained for some time before the markets would respond.
The U.S. sent eight F-117A "stealth" fighters to Kuwait to augment U.S. firepower already in the Gulf.
Traders characterized volume as moderate and said buying was broad-based.
"Any pullbacks held and they closed on a pretty strong note," the trader said of December S&Ps.
Bonds gleaned support before stocks' open from a rise in the latest weekly jobless claims to 338,000 in the week ended September 7 from a revised 317,000 in the previous week.
The Atlanta Fed industry business activity index was reported at 4.0 in August versus a revised -1.2 in July.
September Nikkei 225 futures expired in afternoon trading at 20,515.0, down 5.0.

December S&P 500s closed up 5.10 pts to 678.10, Value Lines firmed 4.10 to 631.50, Midcap 400s added 1.80 pts to 237.95, NYSE Composite firmed 2.30 to 363.10, and December Nikkei 225 were up 5.0 to 20,550.0.
